scope: Actual Unreal/host/controller/Windows scenarios; no rows run in this source-delivery environment.

tests.procedure: Use the retained host without a Sprint component.
tests.expected: Movement stays host-owned. Sprint mode is disabled; other available options and campaign startup still work.

tests.procedure: Add one Sprint component with opt-in false; then enable only after real routing and restart.
tests.expected: No speed changes when disabled. With explicit correct routing the sprint option becomes available.

tests.procedure: Add two Sprint components on the actual character.
tests.expected: Neither is initialized by UI; no competing speed ownership; an options diagnostic is visible.

tests.procedure: Place the component on a controller/director or unpossessed pawn and try initialization.
tests.expected: Initialization refuses; no player or movement component is invented.

tests.procedure: Test defaults, valid custom values, nonfinite values, walk below 100, sprint below walk, and sprint above 1500.
tests.expected: Valid tuning is captured at initialization; invalid tuning is refused without a speed write.

tests.procedure: Wire actual aggregate state. Release Shift after entering gameplay, then press/hold/release while walking.
tests.expected: Cap changes 330 -> 520 -> 330 once; actual motion follows host input/physics; no stamina drain.

tests.procedure: Repeat using controller-only menus and left-stick click.
tests.expected: Same intentional Hold behavior, without needing keyboard input.

tests.procedure: Select Toggle and explicitly apply; move with the stick, press Sprint, release Sprint, press again.
tests.expected: First press selects 520 cap; release preserves selection; second intentional press selects 330 cap.

tests.procedure: Enable Toggle and stop all movement input while continuing real released Sprint samples.
tests.expected: Character stops by host physics. Toggle does not inject a movement direction or act as auto-run.

tests.procedure: Hold Shift and left-stick click together; release only one, then both.
tests.expected: Aggregate state stays down until both are up; no spurious release or second toggle.

tests.procedure: Deliver duplicate aggregate samples in one frame, and repeated down samples across frames.
tests.expected: Only the first sample of a frame is accepted. Holding never repeatedly toggles.

tests.procedure: Press and release within one polling frame, then make a later deliberate press.
tests.expected: Document sampled-state behavior: a pulse not observed is not replayed. No queued future sprint.

tests.procedure: Open and close Pause, Inventory, Journal, Transcript and Settings while holding Sprint.
tests.expected: Sprint intent cancels on permission change. Returning while held never resumes sprint; actual release and a later press are needed.

tests.procedure: Open and close a blocker between two Sprint ticks.
tests.expected: Changed bridge revision still invalidates sprint; no hidden latched toggle survives.

tests.procedure: Pause through the real host, then resume while Sprint is held.
tests.expected: Observed pause disables sprint; resume requires real release and a later press. External pause between samples is not claimed observable without a revision change.

tests.procedure: Use New and Continue while sprint was selected previously.
tests.expected: New epoch resets active sprint. Saved preference mode persists independently, not the transient sprint request.

tests.procedure: Apply an independent controller movement ignore count while sprinting; release that owner correctly.
tests.expected: Sprint cancels; component does not release or reset the other owner’s locks.

tests.procedure: Jump or walk off an edge with Sprint held/toggled, then land.
tests.expected: Observed non-walking mode cancels sprint. Landing requires release/repress; velocity is not forcibly zeroed. Record actual lateral-speed/deceleration behavior.

tests.procedure: Exercise host crouch, flying/custom/swimming or disabled movement as deliberate diagnostics.
tests.expected: Sprint request is disabled outside upright non-crouched MOVE_Walking; no new traversal system or MaxWalkSpeedCrouched change occurs.

tests.procedure: Enter a safety hazard with Sprint held or toggled and complete safe return.
tests.expected: Recovery controls movement as before. Sprint does not resume on arrival; inventory, mission and receipts are unchanged.

tests.procedure: Stop forwarding actual Sprint samples for more than two frames while component ticks; then resume while held.
tests.expected: Speed returns to walk. Input is not rearmed until a true released sample on a later eligible frame, then a later press.

tests.procedure: Test 30/60/120 FPS and long frame hitches, including paused UI transitions.
tests.expected: No delta-time accumulation or toggle repeats. Two-frame lease changes wall-clock duration with FPS; record actual behavior, not an FPS-independence guarantee.

tests.procedure: During an active binding, change MaxWalkSpeed to a distinct value from a separate test owner.
tests.expected: Sprint disables, logs and exposes a diagnostic. The foreign value is preserved; no fight between writers or campaign reset.

tests.procedure: End UI/component lifetime while it still owns its speed; repeat after a foreign speed edit.
tests.expected: Owned original speed is restored only while still owned. Tick prerequisites are removed; foreign edits are preserved.

tests.procedure: Replace/destroy the fixed pawn or movement component during play.
tests.expected: No automatic pawn rebinding; sprint reports lifetime failure when observed and restores only owned state. Other campaign lifecycle rules still apply.

tests.procedure: Use normal tick order, then deliberately violate it or disable the Sprint tick in a disposable test.
tests.expected: Normal controller->Sprint->movement order works. Disabled/unexecuted component ticks cannot police an unobserved stale speed; remove/ReleaseOptions before disabling. Record this host violation, not a claimed recovery.

tests.procedure: Change Hold/Toggle, use Back, Defaults, session-only apply and explicit save through keyboard and gamepad.
tests.expected: Back discards draft; Defaults only changes available fields; session-only does not write; verified save persists the mode.

tests.procedure: Edit mode, then invalidate the sprint consumer before Apply.
tests.expected: Changed mode is not applied silently without the consumer. Reopen options to review available fields.

tests.procedure: Back up real preferences; load the frozen M1.6 fixture in the actual platform options slot.
tests.expected: Original five values and generation load; mode defaults Hold; a legacy-format notice appears; no file is rewritten during load.

tests.procedure: Explicitly save Toggle after loading valid legacy preferences.
tests.expected: Only the inactive slot receives schema 2, generation+1 and exact verified bytes; original legacy slot stays unchanged.

tests.procedure: Load legacy+new slots with distinct/equal generations, then test supported corruption and unsupported future schema.
tests.expected: Highest unambiguous supported generation wins. Equality/future schema/read errors block writes; corrupt newer slot may recover legacy Hold with notice.

tests.procedure: Inject write-before/after, corrupt readback and unreadable readback while upgrading disposable preferences.
tests.expected: Previous live values and previous valid slot remain. Further preference writes block; relaunch resolves whether new bytes reached disk.

tests.procedure: Save campaigns, switch campaigns, relaunch and inspect option/catalogue data.
tests.expected: No preference record appears as campaign; no inventory/mission data enters preferences; active sprint never restores from disk.

tests.procedure: Inspect every options row/command at 100% and 150% text at 1920x1080 and 1280x720.
tests.expected: Six fields and disabled reasons scroll and remain operable; actual focus/preview/back behavior is recorded.

tests.procedure: Package the actual systems room and complete New -> pickups -> storage -> repair -> transcript -> safe return -> verified save -> relaunch -> Continue.
tests.expected: Coherent campaign and retained mode; no lost/duplicated items. A real launched Windows package and evidence are required.
